attributes.nuance_translation: A phrase that expresses when the speaker thinks that (A) is bound to be true.

attributes.body:
はず, coming from the kanji 筈（はず）, is a word in Japanese that is very similar to 'bound' in English. This means that it expresses something that the speaker is 'quite sure is true', but cannot confirm. The most common translations of はず are 'bound to be (A)', and 'should be (A)'.

As はず is a noun, it may be used in any place that a noun would usually be used. It will often be followed by だ, or です.

Caution

Despite はず sometimes being translated as 'should', this is only when you think that something 'should be true', and cannot be used when making suggestions/giving advice. Due to this, 'bound' is the more accurate translation of 筈（はず）, in almost all situations.

Fun Fact

The だ (or です) in はずだ may be omitted. This usually makes はず sound a little less certain, like 'bound to be (A)... probably'. In the same way, speakers may sometimes add はず to the end of their sentences in a similar way to 多分（たぶん）, in order to show that they are not 100% certain about whether what they just said is accurate or not.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar
[AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.description: はず Should / Supposed To in Japanese
Using 「はず」 to describe an expectation

attributes.body: はずだ expresses an assumption or expectation based on reason or context, e.g. 雨が降るはずだ ('It should rain.'). In contrast, べきではない expresses a strong sense of moral or social obligation not to do something, e.g. 嘘をつくべきではない ('You shouldn't lie.').

first_relatable.title: はずだ
first_relatable.meaning: Bound to (be), Expected to (be), Should be (able)

second_relatable.title: べきではない
second_relatable.meaning: Should not, Must not , Ought not to

attributes.body: These forms are opposites. はずだ expresses positive expectation, as in 来るはずだ ('He should come.'), while はずがない strongly denies a possibility based on logic or knowledge, as in 来るはずがない ('There's no way he'll come.'). Both are grounded in reasoning, but the conclusions differ.

first_relatable.title: はずだ
first_relatable.meaning: Bound to (be), Expected to (be), Should be (able)

second_relatable.title: はずがない
second_relatable.meaning: Hardly possible, Cannot be, Highly unlikely, Improbable

attributes.body: はずだ and べき can both be translated as 'should', but they differ in nuance. はずだ expresses an expectation based on evidence or reasoning, like 明日来るはずだ ('He should come tomorrow.'). In contrast, べき expresses obligation or social correctness, as in 来るべきだ ('You should come.').

first_relatable.title: はずだ
first_relatable.meaning: Bound to (be), Expected to (be), Should be (able)

attributes.body: Both can describe future events, but differ in source. はずだ shows the speaker's expectation, like 来るはずだ ('He should come.'). ことになっている refers to something officially decided, often outside the speaker's control. For example, 来ることになっている ('It has been decided that he will come.')

first_relatable.title: ことになっている
first_relatable.meaning: To be expected to, To be scheduled to

second_relatable.title: はずだ
second_relatable.meaning: Bound to (be), Expected to (be), Should be (able)

attributes.body: つもりだ is used to express personal intentions or plans, similar to 'I hope to' or 'I intend to' in English. In contrast, はずだ expresses an expectation or belief that something will happen, based on logic or evidence. While つもりだ is subjective and often refers to the speaker's own plans, はずだ is more objective and is used for expectations about others or events outside the speaker's control.

first_relatable.title: つもりだ
first_relatable.meaning: To plan to, To intend to

second_relatable.title: はずだ
second_relatable.meaning: Bound to (be), Expected to (be), Should be (able)

attributes.body: Both express logical conclusions, but with different emphasis. はずだ conveys expectation or prediction, as in 来るはずだ ('He should come.'). わけだ explains a reason behind something known or observed, like 来るわけだ ('So that's why he's coming.'). はずだ leans future-oriented, わけだ explanatory.

first_relatable.title: わけだ
first_relatable.meaning: For that reason, No wonder, As you'd expect, Naturally, Thus, This is why

second_relatable.title: はずだ
second_relatable.meaning: Bound to (be), Expected to (be), Should be (able)

attributes.body: はずだ conveys a specific expectation or prediction based on current evidence, like 雨が降るはずだ ('It should rain.'). ものだ expresses a general rule or common tendency, like 雨は春によく降るものだ ('It often rains in spring.'). The former is situational, while the latter is habitual or cultural.

first_relatable.title: はずだ
first_relatable.meaning: Bound to (be), Expected to (be), Should be (able)

second_relatable.title: ものだ
second_relatable.meaning: Supposed to, Should, That's the way it is

attributes.body: はずだ expresses confident expectation, as in 雨が降るはずだ ('It should rain.'). たらいい and といい express hope or desire without implying it will happen, e.g. 雨が降るといい ('I hope it rains.'). The difference lies in expectation vs. wish. Thus, といい is often used even when the speaker is not confident the thing will happen.

first_relatable.title: はずだ
first_relatable.meaning: Bound to (be), Expected to (be), Should be (able)

second_relatable.title: たらいい・といい
second_relatable.meaning: It would be nice if, It would be good if, Should, I hope

attributes.body: はずだ indicates something is expected based on information or logic, as in 行けるはずだ ('I should be able to go.'). ばいい expresses hope or a hypothetical good outcome, like 行ければいい ('It'd be nice if I could go.'). One is based on reasoning, the other on desire.

first_relatable.title: はずだ
first_relatable.meaning: Bound to (be), Expected to (be), Should be (able)

second_relatable.title: ばいい
second_relatable.meaning: Can, Should, It'd be good if
